tasks_completed.rationale: Single-source-of-truth replacement for the rejected 30-bespoke-per-symptom hook stack (spec 5.2). Implements: (1) jsonschema validation with cross-file $ref registry, (2) forbidden-token grep on data using AC2's reformulated regex with the principled exclusions for modification-log.json/plan-skeleton.json/requirements-skeleton.json, (3) stock-image-URL grep (unsplash/picsum/placeholder.com/via.placeholder.com/loremflickr/placekitten), (4) HTTP-protocol image_url grep, (5) key=AIzaSy WARN-only grep per user 5.1, (6) HTML-rendered scan via --html-also <file>. Two CLI modes (data-only and data+html). Per architect concern_4 honors IMAGE_FETCH_STATUS=FAILED env signal. Schema-strictness toggleable via --strict-schema (orchestrator W1 directive: 'verifier must accept current state initially' — schema findings default to WARN until W2 lands M2/M3 cleanups; deploy gate passes --strict-schema explicitly).

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Verifier is a 6-in-1 check unifying schema validation (jsonschema with $ref registry), four pattern grep checks (forbidden tokens, stock URLs, http://, key=AIzaSy), HTML rendered scan, IMAGE_FETCH_STATUS env signal, and CLI argument parsing. The orchestrator-mandated quality gate (max 30-line functions, max 3-level nesting) required splitting the 6 checks plus their helpers into ~20 small functions. The new file size of ~480 lines reflects (a) the breadth of the 6-in-1 scope, (b) per-finding location + remediation hint output, and (c) explicit helper decomposition mandated by the project's pretool-quality-gate.py (max 30 lines per function, max nesting 3). Wire-up edits in generate-and-deploy.sh add ~24 lines (two RED-banner blocks). Total <500 lines, well under the 800-line file threshold.

implementation_notes: Quality gate (~/.claude/hooks/pretool-quality-gate.py: max 30-line functions, max 3-level nesting) blocked the initial monolithic implementation 3 times. Refactored into ~20 small helpers per the gate's enforced limits. This is why the file is ~480 lines (the algorithmic core would be ~150 lines; the rest is scaffolding for the gate's mandated decomposition).

Schema-strictness toggle resolves a tension: the orchestrator's W1 acceptance directive 'verifier must accept current state initially' conflicts with the spec's deploy-blocking semantics. Resolution: schema findings default to WARN (lenient — passes today's canary even with W2 not yet landed), and the deploy gate explicitly passes --strict-schema (the strict mode). After W2 merges and the canary is clean, lenient default can be flipped to strict in a future cycle.

BA spec's 'currently 0 keys in canary trip' (Acceptance Evidence § AC11) was specifically about data/<plan>/images.json count being 0. Across all canary JSON, the count is 24 (same root URLs leaked into meals.json image_url fields). Per user 5.1 these are WARN-only, so the verifier's behavior is correct (exit 0).

BA spec's reformulated AC2 forbidden-token regex was used verbatim — the corrected version with single grouped alternation `"(...)"` so each token is properly bracketed, plus the principled exclusions for modification-log.json/plan-skeleton.json/requirements-skeleton.json.
